traditions.d: Korean earthenware jars, unglazed or dark-brown glazed, used for fermenting and storing kimchi, soy sauce and pastes.
traditions.tech: Coil-built earthenware fired at 600–700 °C unglazed or over 1100 °C with dark-brown glaze; slightly porous body lets ferments breathe.
traditions.auth: Hand-thrown body, dark brown glaze, breathable walls; look for size names and workshop marks rather than mass-moulded uniformity.

traditions.d: Japanese vegetable pickling in salt, brine or a fermented rice-bran bed, using tubs, pressing stones and screw-top pickle presses.
traditions.tech: Vegetables pressed under weight in salt or buried in a daily-stirred rice-bran (nuka) bed.
traditions.mat: Wooden or ceramic tubs, enamel or plastic nukadoko containers, pickle presses
traditions.auth: Traditional nukadoko is kept alive by daily hand-stirring; pressing containers are judged by lid pressure and capacity rather than brand.
